To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

protease inhibitor (PI)-containing regimens are more effective than nucleoside analog (NA) alone in suppressing persistent HIV-1 RNA replication and proviral DNA synthesis in lymphoid tissue of HIV-1-infected individuals.

the protease inhibitor lopinavir-ritonavir (LPV/r) and the non-nucleoside reverse transcriptase inhibitor efavirenz (EFV) suppress HIV-1 replication more efficiently than nucleoside reverse transcriptasase inhibitors in lymphoid tissue of HIV-infected patients on ART.

the use of protease inhibitor (PI)-containing regimens in HIV-1-infected subjects with low plasma HIV-1 RNA levels (viral load) results in the suppression of HIV-1 replication and a decrease in the number of infected CD4 T cells in lymphoid tissue (LT).
In summary, our research is concerned with

the development and characterization of a novel, non-viral gene transfer system based on the delivery of DNA into mammalian cells by the use of the bacterial enzyme endonuclease I-SceI and the homologous recognition sequence (I-SceI).
the development of new methods for the synthesis and study of the properties of the compounds of the general formula: R1 = R2 = H, R1 = H, R2 = alkyl; R1 = alkyl, R2 = H.
the development of novel protease inhibitors for the treatment of HIV/AIDS.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the use of a combination of antiretroviral drugs is the only effective method of suppressing HIV-1.

the protease inhibitor-containing regiments are more effective than the nucleoside analogs alone in the suppression and eradication of persistent HIV- 1 replication in lymphocytes and lymphoid tissue.
the results of this study indicate a trend towards a higher efficacy of PI-containing regimens in the suppression of HIV-1 replication and preservation of CD4 cell count in lymphoid tissues.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the protease inhibitor-containing regiments have a greater suppression of HIV-1 replication compared to the nucleoside analogue regiments.

the results of this study support the hypothesis that the protease inhibitor (PI)-containing regimens suppress HIV-1 replication better than nucleoside analogue (NA)-only regimens in lymphoid tissues.

protease inhibitor (PI)-containing antiretroviral (ARV) regimens suppress HIV-1 replication better than nucleoside analogs (NRTIs) alone in lymphoid tissue, and that PI-containing regimens are more potent in suppressing replication than NRTIs alone in lymphoid cells, but that PI-containing regiments are more likely to select for resistant HIV-1 in lymphoid tissue than are NRTIs alone.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the HIV reservoir in lymphoid tissues is a dynamic and heterogeneous population of cells.
HIV-1 infection is associated with increased levels of circulating miRNAs.
HIV-1 infection in the CNS is a complex process that is not simply driven by the amount of virus in the blood.
